---
title: "A short tip with a long form"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Keep the tip to one line, and put the rest behind a "More" button in the same tip. Most readers never press it, and the few
who do get the whole story.

```{r}
library(hovercraft)

tip_on(
  htmltools::tags$button("Run"),
  "Runs the **check**",
  more = "Checks every column and prints a summary. Takes about a minute on the full data."
)
```

The tip stays open and stays on its side while it grows, and "Less" folds it back. The next time it opens, it is short
again. With the focus on the item or the pointer resting on it, the `M` key does what the button does, except in a text
field. A pinned tip has the same buttons. The default button needs no pin and no `id`.

`more` takes words, a `tip_template()`, or a `tip_more()`. Words and a template are the same as `tip_more()` with its
defaults.

## When the long form shows

`tip_more(on = )` chooses:

| `on =` | The long form shows |
|---|---|
| `"button"` (default) | when the reader presses "More" |
| `"hover"` | at once, with the short form |
| `"pin"` | when the tip is pinned (the tag needs `pin` and an `id`) |
| `"click"` | on a click on the item, with no button (not for a control, and not for a table, where a click selects a row) |

```{r}
tip_on(
  htmltools::tags$span("ADSL", tabindex = "0"),
  "Subject-level data",
  more = tip_more("One row per subject. Built from the raw demographics.", on = "click")
)
```

## The button

These apply only with the default `on = "button"`; with another moment they stop with an error.

- `label =` changes the words: one string for "More", or `c(more = "Show all", less = "Show less")`.
- `as = "link"` draws an italic text link in place of a button, and `where = "start"` or `"end"` puts the control on the
  side you choose. A link sits at the start by default, a button at the end.
- `pin = TRUE` makes the button pin the tip too, so the long form stays when the pointer leaves. It needs a tip that can
  pin: `pin = TRUE` and an `id` on the tag, or `rows = tip_spec(pin = TRUE)` and an `id` on `tip_table()`.

```{r}
tip_on(
  htmltools::tags$div("ADAE", tabindex = "0"),
  "Adverse events",
  more = tip_more(
    "Coded with the current dictionary. Serious events are flagged.",
    as = "link",
    pin = TRUE,
    label = c(more = "Show details", less = "Show less")
  ),
  pin = TRUE,
  id = "adae"
)
```

## In a table, and with records

The long form fills in `{{ field }}` placeholders from the tip's record, or from the row in a table, the same as the short
form does:

```{r}
scores <- data.frame(team = c("Reds", "Blues"), wins = c(12, 9), coach = c("A. Reviewer", "B. Reviewer"))

tip_table(
  DT::datatable(scores),
  rows = tip_spec("{{ team }}: {{ wins }} wins", more = "Coach: {{ coach }}")
)
```

With `events = "pin"`, a pinned tip that grows sends `input$<id>_pin` with `state = "updated"`. A hover tip that grows
sends nothing.

`more` as words or a template is stable. `tip_more()` and its arguments are experimental in 0.1.0, so a later 0.x release
may change them. Every option is a section of [the book](the-book.html), with a figure to try. For the rest of what a tip
holds, see [Get started](hovercraft.html).
